title: Sinhala / Tamil New Year Celebration - 2017
html:
Sinhala / Tamil New Year Celebration - 2017

This is a past event. This event took place on April 15, 2017

What is the Sinhala / Tamil New Year Celebration?

Sinhala and Tamil New Year, generally known as Aluth Avurudda in Sri Lanka, is an event celebrated by Sri Lankans. This event is celebrated every year in April. Wikipedia has an excellent introduction to this traditional event.

New Year Celebration at SIBC

SIBC is conducting a Buddha pooja and Seth Pirith chanting and an offering of blessings for the Sinhala and Tamil New year. The ceremony will be held on Saturday, 15-Apr 2017 starting at 4.45PM at the SIBC temple premises in Tukwila, Washington. Events will finish by 7pm.

5.00PM : Buddha Pooja

Resident monks will also conduct a Buddha pooja and we have an opportunity offer our gratitude to Buddha, Dhamma and Sangha. Children will have the opportunity offer traditional greetings with Betel leaves to the monks, parents and elders and get blessings for the new year.

6.00PM : Pirith chanting

Pirith is the Sinhala word for the Pali word “paritta”, which means protection. Buddhists believe that recitation and contemplation of the words of the Buddha protects them from bad influences and promotes peace of mind and love. Seth pirith is a special form of pirith chanting conducted in Sri Lanka to offer blessings.

6.45PM : Sri Lankan traditional kiribath and snack foods

These religious events will be followed by a traditional Sri Lankan pot luck comprising of Kiribath (Milk rice), and other snacks. Please sign up to bring food items to share with your friends. (Web link will be sent soon)

Notes

Attire / What to bring

You may dress in traditional Sri Lankan clothes or simply what’s comfortable. Please note that it’s customary to wear light clothes when visiting a Buddhist temple. Please bring flowers if you wish to participate in the Buddha pooja. You may bring a few Betel leaves if you would like your children to take part in traditional greeting.

Can we invite our friends?

All SIBC events, including Sinhala and Tamil New year celebrations are open to everyone regardless of race or religion. Reserve the date and tell your friends. We look forward to seeing you there.

title: Special Campaign - SIBC Bathroom Project
html:
SIBC is planning to create an additional bathroom for the benefit of the monks as well as the visting public. This webpage highlights the details of this project.

To pledege a donation, please use the donation form below or visit it directly here.

Q & A

Is this part of the larger kitchen and residence expansion project?

Currently the garage has been converted into a Monk’s residence with the addition of 3 bedrooms. The kitchen and residence expansion project is the long term plan to replace the garage with a 2-story building. Longer term plans is in concept stage see initial sketches below. The project would take several years to plan and complete.

As part of the longer-term plan there are plans to build monk’s bedrooms and bathrooms in the ground floor. The kitchen and dining area would be located in the upper floor which would be on the same level as the Dhamma sala. The bathroom being constructed now, would be included in the longer-term plan and will reduce the need build additional bathrooms in ground floor

What’s included in the bathroom remodeling plan?

Removal of the temporary toilet in the basement including tearing down and removal of debris (basement will be used for storage only). Construction of enclosure walls and creating the bathroom 7.4 x 7.8 feet Heating, Plumbing and electrical wiring and fixing bathroom fittings (shower has already been donated) Digging and removal of dirt.

Will there be additional expenses we have to incur in sewer connections?

None - the remodeled bathroom will use the existing sewer connection.

What are the dimensions?

Bathroom is 7ft 6 inches x 7ft x 8 inches. See images below for the details

Are permits required?

No permits are required since this is a remodeling of the existing toilet in the basement. This was consulted with the architect of the project.

How can members donate money and items for this project?

The bathtub and shower has already been donated by devotees The contractors quotation includes the sink, toilet and all other bathroom fittings.

What is the cost?

$25,000 to be paid to the contractor on completion.

When can the work begin? how long will the project take

Contract can begin with approval from Venerable Loku Hamuduruwo with the agreement from Dayaka sabha. Project is expected to take 3 weeks.

What will happen to the staircase that is being used as a shortcut to take items from the residence to Dhamma sala?

The bathroom is being constructed in the landing area of the stairs - stairs will not be accessible in the current location and needs to be removed Contractors will attach the staircase next to the garage (behind the first parking stall)

What about the front entrance to the residence and adjoining building?

Stairs to the residence as well as the basement will remain. Front foyer will be enclosed with a French-door so that the bathroom door and the stairs to the residence will remain covered.

title: Buddha Pooja and Blessings for School - 2019
html:
Buddha Pooja and Blessings for School - 2019

This is a past event. This event took place on August 31, 2019

Buddha Pooja and Blessings for School - 2019

Buddha pooja is conducted to offer obeisance to Buddhas including the present Goutama Buddha. This ancient devotional practice increases our affinity with infinite virtues of Buddhas and deepens and our commitment on the Path.

On completion of the Buddha pooja, Resident monks will also chant Seth pirith and bless the children for the up-coming school year. On conclusion of Seth pirith, you should encourage your children to get a pirith noola, a blessed string, from the resident monks. A pirith noola, or a Buddhist bracelet, it is a visual reminder that you’ve taken a vow to follow the five percepts and to follow the noble eightfold path. A pirith noola is also a reminder that you have received a blessing to be strong and to stay focused on good behavior.

Please bring your children for this pooja and encourage them to get a pirith noola.

The program is as follows

  • Arrival, networking - 5.00 PM
  • Commencement of Buddha pooja and Seth pirith- 5.30PM
  • Conclusion of events - 7.30PM

This pooja is sponsored by Dinesh and Ganga Uduwana. They cordially invite your presence at the pooja and to join your Dhamma friends for refreshments afterwards.

title: Special Dhamma Desana - 2018 August
html:
Special Dhamma Desana - 2018 August

This is a past event. This event took place on August 01, 2018

English Dhamma talk and discussion with Bhante Phillip Ṭhānavuḍḍho

We are pleased to announce that Bhante Phillip Ṭhānavuḍḍho has accepted our invitation for a Dhamma talk at the Sarana International Buddhist Center (SIBC) in Tukwila, Washington.

During the Vassana period from July to October, Buddhist monks around the world reduce travel and reside in their local temples to focus on spiritual development. This practice, dating back 2500 years, started in India during the time of Buddha. Bhante Phillip Ṭhānavuḍḍho is observing the Vassana period in the Wat Atammayatarama in Woodinville, Washington.

Bhante is a pali prefix we use to address a Buddhist Monk similar to the way we address strangers with respect as Sir or Madam. You may address him as Bhante or Bhante Phra Phiilip.

He was raised in Washington, D.C. and became a Buddhist at age 13, attending meditation classes at the Washington Buddhist Vihara. He ordained in Sri Lanka in 2013, after one year of intense training as an anagārika and another year as a samanēra, at the Na-Uyana Aranya forest temple, under the late Ven. Ariyadhamma Mahathera. In 2015, Phra Phillip relocated to Rayong, Thailand and re-ordained at Wat Lahanrai (วัดละหารไร่), living at a nearby forest temple. He studied for one year in Myanmar in 2017.

Before becoming a Buddhist monk, Bhante Phra Phillip worked as a lawyer in Washington, D.C. and did legal translation for four years in Sichuan Province, China. He is fluent in English, Spanish, Latin, and can speak basic Thai and Standard Mandarin Chinese (to HSK-2 level). He holds a dual Doctorate (JD/Ph.D) in Law and Philosophy from Indiana University and Georgetown University.

Background

In year 2024, SIBC aims to enhance our temple by building a concrete wall to replace the existing fence. The estimated cost for this project is $35,000 to $40,000. We have established a dedicated capital account to collect funds exclusively for this project, ensuring full transparency. All raised funds will be used solely for the wall construction, while all Katina expenses will be covered by two patron families.

SIBC serves as a vital cultural and community hub for the Sri Lankan community, as well as a place of worship for Buddhists. Many lasting friendships and community bonds have been formed here. It is also a place where our children can connect with their heritage and take pride in their roots. In keeping with traditional Sri Lankan aesthetics, we plan to adorn the wall with cloud-shaped structures (“Walakulu Bamma”).

2024 Project: Concrete Wall Construction

  • Location: Along 51st Ave S, replacing the current fence.
  • Dimensions: Approximately 160 ft in length.
  • Current Gate: Will remain in place.
  • Cloud Adornments: Not included in the initial construction but will be considered in future enhancements (phase 2).
  • Durability: 50 year life, low maintenance, ability to support cloud structure

Project Estimates and Timeline

  • Cost: Initial estimates are $35,000+.
  • Timeline: Start date upon securing full funding. The project is expected to take 4-6 weeks once commenced.

Project Funding

  • Planning and Management: Volunteers from the Kodituwakku and Ratnayake families.
  • Funding Sources: Donations, fundraising events, and volunteer efforts.

  • Fundraising Events: Few planned are below. Seeking more community leaders/events:

    • Wall Project Pledge (Ven Sanga Saba, all friends of SIBC)
    • Food Festival (Dayaka Sabha)
    • Community Bowling Night (Chandima & Dayantha)

How You Can Help

Pledge your wall donation here

  • Pay via : sibc.buildingfund@gmail.com.
  • Participate in Fundraisers: Join and support community fundraising events.
  • Lead a Fundraising : Help SIBC reach $40,000 goal; organize & raise funds.

Your support is crucial to making this vision a reality. Together, we can build a lasting legacy for our community.

FAQ (last updated : August 2024)

Purpose - Why are we focusing on this project?

Is the fund raising for Katina?

All raised funds will be used solely for the wall construction, while all Katina expenses will be covered by Kodituwakku and Ratnayake families who are patrons for Katina.

Who proposed this project for 2024?

Ven. Pangananda and the Sanga proposed this as it presents a unique opportunity to integrate Sri Lankan cultural aesthetics to SIBC. In keeping with traditional Sri Lankan aesthetics, we plan to adorn the wall with cloud-shaped structures (“Walakulu Bamma”). Other projects proposed by Dayaka Saba were also considered.

I am not a devotee, why are you reaching out to me?

SIBC serves as a vital cultural and community hub for the Sri Lankan community, as well as a place of worship for Buddhists. Many lasting friendships and community bonds have been formed here. It is also a place where our children can connect with their heritage and take pride in their roots to Sri Lanka. eg. During Easter bombing crisis in Sri Lanka SIBC hosted a community gathering with Ven Pangnanda’s leadership for all faiths and nationalities. SIBC throughout the year hosts secular events such as Avrudu, community lunches etc.

Is this the most urgent project for SIBC?

Currently there is urgent need to relace the broken fence. This presents a unique opportunity for SIBC to bring a Sri Lankan Cultural look currently missing. Furthermore this effort is laying the foundation for future large projects with the creation of a separate account for capital projects and expanding donation options to DAF and stocks.

What the role of Katina patrons in this project?

Ven. Pangananda asked that the 2 families lead this project to completion before October with the help of entire community, Sanga. He asked that they manage all stakeholders (including contractors, donors etc) so that Ven. can be free to concentrate on his religious and philanthropic activities here and in Sri Lanka. They may reach out to you on behalf of Sanga to ask for help.

Project Details - What are we building?

Why did you decide on a wall, which is more expensive than a fence?

Few options were considered are below.

  • Composite fence ($30k) -no cultural look,15 year life, easy maintenance, residential look
  • Aluminum fence with laser cut cloud ($35k) - 35 year life, easy maintenance, industrial look
  • Concrete wall that can hold a cloud ($40k) - 50 year life, low maintenance, cultural look

While upfront cost is high, over a longer time horizon concrete wall offers better value as well as cultural aesthetics. Hence Ven Pangananada decided on a concrete wall.

Why is the wall 4 feet?

This will avoids lengthy permitting process required in City of Tukwila which can take up to 6-12 months.

Why do you need funds by August 31, we usually donate for Katina in October?

The project needs $40k to start & engage a contractor. Contractors recommend we complete before the rains start. Hence construction need to start in Sep or earlier, which means we need all funds to be in place before Aug 31. Ven Pangananga, Katina Patrons, Dayaka Saba have pledged not to raise loans for this project. These funds are for the wall not Katina. Once the project funds are met, you may continue to donate to SIBC general fund or future building fund projects throughout the remaining year and beyond.

What happens if we don’t collect $40k before Aug 31?

The fund raising will continue until fund need is met (beyond Oct 2024 however long it takes) and contractor will be engaged when the funds are cleared and available. At that time an appropriate begin date will be established with contractor based on weather. Project will require new quotes (likely higher cost) if it slips the Sep projection.

Donations - How do we plan to raise the money?

$40k is a fairly large fund target for such a short amount of time, how are we planning to meet it ? While this is a medium size project for Seattle area (eg. bathroom project cost $30k last year), it is a large amount for a short window. We plan to raise funds as follows :

  • $6k from 2 community events planned
  • $5-10k from small/medium contributions $1-999
  • $24-31k from large contributions $1000-5000+

We encourage everyone to contribute what you are comfortable. We may add other events or extend to next year if we don’t meet our goal in time.

I don’t have zelle, can I direct transfer from my bank ?

Yes you can. Please transfer to Building Fund Account :

  • [Bank details omitted pending SIBC review]
  • [Bank details omitted pending SIBC review]

I don’t have cash to donate, can I donate stocks towards the fund ?

Yes you can. If you have highly appreciated stocks you can avoid paying capital gains taxes as well as get a tax deduction on donation. Please allow for 5-10 business days to clear. Please contact Chandima Kodituwakku for more information ([Personal phone omitted pending review]).

I want to give to the SIBC general fund instead. Can I still do that during this time ?

Absolutely, we welcome all donations, monthly recurring or one time. More information here https://sibc-tukwila.org/donations/

Can you use Employer Matching funds to pay for the project ?

Employer matching funds through Benevity can only be used for community and civil actions such as volunteering etc. They cannot be used for construction or religious activities. If your employer matches we encourage you to submit your donation receipt to request match or report volunteer hrs. For more information contact Deepal Jayasinghe.

If I am coming to the food festival and bowling event, do I still need to donate ?

Food festival and bowling events are secular (non religious) events. Please attend and bring your friends to extend the reach for our community. These are charitable fundraising events (you get something in return), not donations. Donations are still open to you at any level you are comfortable and much appreciated. Pledge & pay through Aug 30 here. https://tinyurl.com/SIBCwallDonate
